newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Thursday.

"The interbank rate eased slightly again today but there was still little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were steady to slightly lower but bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.53/1.48 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 1.55/1.50 percent but one-year was unchanged from Wednesday's yield of 1.73/1.68 percent.
Among bonds, April 1998 ended at S$99.55/99.60 against Wednesday's close of S$99.48/99.58, September 2001 at S$96.73/96.78 versus S$96.67/96.72 and June 2003 at S$94.73/94.78 from S$94.66/94.71.
The interbank rate eased to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent against Wednesday's 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent.
